question: What is the structure of Uganda's health and medical sector and how are health providers regulated?
answer: Uganda's healthcare system comprises public/government facilities (approx. 66% of service outlets) and private providers (34%), including Private Not-for-Profit (PNFP) faith-based facilities (governed by the Uganda Catholic Medical Bureau UCMB, Uganda Protestant Medical Bureau UPMB, Uganda Orthodox Medical Bureau UOMB, and Uganda Muslim Medical Bureau UMMB), Private-for-Profit commercial healthcare providers (PFPs), and Traditional and Complementary Medicine Practitioners (TCMPs). All health operators must be registered with URSB for business names, licensed by the National Drug Authority (NDA), accredited by professional councils (Uganda Medical and Dental Practitioners Council UMDPC or Uganda Nurses and Midwives Council UNMC), and registered for taxes with URA.

question: What are the tax obligations and licensing rules for herbal shops in Uganda?
answer: Herbal shops sell medicinal plants, essential oils, seeds, roots, bark, and herbal essences. Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/herbal-shops/, herbal shops must: 1) Register business names with URSB; 2) Obtain an operational permit from the National Drug Authority (NDA); 3) Obtain a local trading license from KCCA or the municipal council; 4) Register for taxes with URA. Sole proprietors with annual turnover between UGX 10M and UGX 150M pay presumptive tax (or standard individual income tax if keeping accounts); larger shops pay standard income tax.

question: What are the regulatory differences and tax rules between pharmacies and drug shops?
answer: Under URA and NDA regulations at https://ura.go.ug/en/pharmacy-and-drug-shops/: 1) Pharmacies are dedicated healthcare establishments where prescribed and compounded medications are dispensed exclusively by a licensed pharmacist; pharmacies are taxed as companies under 30% Corporation Tax, must withhold PAYE for staff earning above the threshold, and account for 6% WHT on non-exempt supplies exceeding UGX 1,000,000; 2) Drug shops are lower-tier retail walk-in outlets authorized to dispense only Class C over-the-counter drugs; drug shops must be located not less than 1.5 km away from any licensed pharmacy and typically pay presumptive tax based on gross sales.

question: What taxes and incentives apply to pharmaceutical manufacturers in Uganda?
answer: Pharmaceutical manufacturers produce, compound, or process prescription drugs. Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/pharmaceutical-manufacturers/: 1) Standard corporate income tax is 30% on net profits, with directors filing returns and staff subject to PAYE; 2) Under the Fifth Schedule of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), pharmaceutical processors enjoy 100% customs duty and tax exemption on imported raw materials for the manufacture of medicaments and packaging materials for medicines; 3) Under the VAT Act and EAC Common External Tariff (CET), syringes, medical autoclaves, and heating/ventilation equipment attract 0% import duty and are exempt from VAT.

question: What tax exemptions and incentives are available for hospitals, medical centers, and specialized healthcare investments?
answer: Under the URA Health and Medical Sector Guide (FY 2021-22) at https://ura.go.ug/en/a-guide-to-taxation-of-the-health-and-medical-sector/: 1) Goods marked with the hospital logo imported for licensed hospitals are exempt from all taxes under the Fifth Schedule EACCMA (shadowless operating theatre lamps, blood freezers, mortuary refrigeration units, wheelchairs, crutches, hospital furniture, ambulances, and examination gloves); 2) Diagnostic equipment (X-ray machines, chemical blood analyzers, ultrasound machines, cardiographic machines, dental drills) attracts 0% import duty under EAC CET and is exempt from VAT; 3) Specialized Hospital Developers investing at least USD 5 million to construct a referral-level hospital offering specialized care receive 100% stamp duty exemption on land transfers/leases/mortgages and VAT exemption on feasibility studies, construction services, and machinery; 4) Medical manufacturers investing USD 10M (foreign) or USD 300,000 (local) in industrial parks receive a 10-year income tax holiday.

question: Where can I download the official URA Health and Medical Sector Taxation Guide?
answer: The official compendium 'A Guide to Taxation of the Health and Medical Sector' (First Edition, 40 pages) is downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2024/02/A-Guide-To-Taxation-of-Health-and-Medical-Sector-FY-2021-22.pdf and published under Tax Education at https://ura.go.ug/en/a-guide-to-taxation-of-the-health-and-medical-sector/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/overview-of-the-mining-sector-2/.
